thread:
ana: Heads-up — ran an nsys pass on the 20ms continuous-batching window canary. Seeing a weird kernel flip around small batch sizes that spikes p50->p99.
matt: ugh. kernel flip as in different kernel chosen by cuBLAS/tuned path or our kernel selector heuristics?
ana: looks like selector + kernel availability interplay. trace shows fused_attention_fast used for batch>=4, but for batch 2-3 it picks matmul+manual softmax path. latency increases for those tiny windows.
perf-bot: automated summary: total GPU time +35% for tiny-window workload; queue_time increased by ~2x for affected traces. full report uploaded: /perf/artifacts/1979002222/nsys-report.qdrep
sophia: can you paste the timeline snippet? interested in kernel durations vs queue gaps.
ana: snippet below (copied from perfetto/nsys timeline):
```
2026-03-17T14:00:00Z  kernel:fused_attn_fast     9.3ms  launch->complete  contiguous
2026-03-17T14:00:01Z  kernel:matmul_dense       38.7ms launch->complete  split across warps
2026-03-17T14:00:01Z  queue_gap                 11.2ms queue->gpu idle
2026-03-17T14:00:02Z  kernel:softmax_manual      6.5ms  launch->complete
```
ana: so when selector picks matmul_dense path we not only get slower kernel but also more queue gaps — likely because of larger kernel startup/streaming behavior.
leo: did you check KV cache hit distribution? small batches might reduce prefix reuse and cause different scheduling of KV sweeps.
ana: yes, kvcache hitrate drops 8% in the tiny-window scenario; I think cache fragmentation + our dispatcher prefetch heuristics are interacting badly.
matt: hypothesis: when batch < 4 we disable certain fused kernels because of occupancy estimates. maybe the heuristic threshold is too high and should consider sequence length & KV cache locality.
sophia: agree. patch idea: compute an effective occupancy metric that includes expected KV reuse (hitrate) and batch size, then prefer fused_attn if occupancy_eff > threshold.
perf-bot: quick numbers from the run:
```
baseline (window 100ms): p50=22ms p99=45ms GPU=21ms
tiny-window (20ms): p50=27ms p99=82ms GPU=28ms
diff: p99 +82% GPU time +33% queue_gap p99 +120%
```
leo: embarrassing but expected. can we reproduce locally with nvprof/ncu? I want a per-kernel occupancy and launch latency breakdown.
ana: I have a smaller repro kernel that triggers the flip; will upload to /tmp/ana/repro_small_batch.tar.gz. nvprof run shows matmul launch overhead ~2.4ms larger due to multiple kernel splits.
matt: next steps:
- ana: share repro, add perfetto full timeline and stack collection (done)
- sophia: prototype occupancy_eff and tweak selector.
- leo: run ncu occupancy and kernel launch telemetry on repro.
- I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow 10am to validate patch impact.
ana: FYI I reverted a canary that used 20ms window to avoid customer impact. keeping canary disabled until fix.
sophia: also adding a unit test that forces tiny windows and asserts selector picks fused path when occupancy_eff would prefer it.
leo: thanks. can someone file a small perf-regression ticket with the attached nsys qdrep and timeline? I'll triage infra side.
matt: I'll open ticket INF-3218 with artifacts.
ana: thanks all :thumbsup:
